Merge an SDTM supplemental domain with its primary domain

Source: R/supp_merge.r
ks_supp_merge.Rd

Transposes a SUPP– dataset from long (one row per variable) to wide and left-joins it onto the primary domain using the appropriate key columns.

Usage

ks_supp_merge(primary, supp, mvars = NULL, get_labels = TRUE, rep_na = FALSE)

Arguments

primary

A data frame or tibble: the primary SDTM domain (e.g. DM, EX).

supp

A data frame or tibble: the corresponding SUPP– domain (e.g. SUPPDM, SUPPEX). Must pass ks_supp_consistency_check.

mvars

Character vector of QNAM values to merge. NULL (default) merges all available variables.

get_labels

Logical; if TRUE (default) attach QLABEL values as column "label" attributes on the merged columns.

rep_na

Logical; if TRUE replace NA in merged columns with "". Default FALSE.

Value

The primary data frame with SUPP variables added as new columns.

Details

The merge strategy depends on IDVAR/IDVARVAL:

Subject-level (noid = TRUE)

All IDVAR/IDVARVAL are blank. The join key is STUDYID + USUBJID.

Record-level (noid = FALSE)

Each row in the SUPP is tied to a specific record in the primary domain. IDVAR names the primary domain variable (e.g. EXSEQ) and IDVARVAL holds its value. When multiple distinct IDVAR values are present, each is processed in a separate join pass.

If get_labels = TRUE and the primary domain was loaded via haven (or another reader that preserves column "label" attributes), the per-variable labels from QLABEL are attached to the newly added columns.

See also

ks_supp_consistency_check

Examples

dm <- data.frame(
  STUDYID = "S1",
  USUBJID = c("01", "02", "03"),
  AGE     = c(34L, 52L, 47L),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
suppdm <- data.frame(
  STUDYID  = "S1",
  USUBJID  = c("01", "02", "03"),
  IDVAR    = "",
  IDVARVAL = "",
  QNAM     = "RACE2",
  QLABEL   = "Race (detail)",
  QVAL     = c("Asian", "White", "Asian"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
ks_supp_merge(dm, suppdm)
#>   STUDYID USUBJID AGE RACE2
#> 1      S1      01  34 Asian
#> 2      S1      02  52 White
#> 3      S1      03  47 Asian
